---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Twenty minutes, two days before the course. Not on the morning of Day 1."
---

You need Python 3.12, git, and either Docker or nothing else at all. There is no
API key to obtain and no account to create.

## The short version

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Docker (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MohammadYusif/llm-application-engineering
cd llm-application-engineering/murshid
docker compose up -d
docker compose run --rm tests            # 165 tests, about 20 seconds
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/ask -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"How do I renew my commercial licence?"}'
```

### macOS / Linux

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MohammadYusif/llm-application-engineering
cd llm-application-engineering/murshid
python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.lock

# terminal one — the course gateway
make gateway

# terminal two
make doctor
make chat
```

### Windows

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/MohammadYusif/llm-application-engineering
cd llm-application-engineering\murshid
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.lock

# terminal one — the course gateway
.\make.ps1 gateway

# terminal two
.\make.ps1 doctor
.\make.ps1 chat
```

`make.ps1` has the same target names as the Makefile. If you have `make` (Git Bash,
WSL, or `scoop install make`), use it instead — everything in these pages is
written as `make <target>`.

:::

## `make doctor` is the contract

```
$ make doctor
murshid doctor

  ✓ python 3.12+ — 3.12.10
  ✓ config loads — 4 routes
  ✓ terminal renders Arabic — كيف أجدد رخصتي التجارية؟
  ✓ prompt registry — 8 versions
  ✓ route primary — course-flagship in 103ms
  ✓ route cheap — course-small in 50ms
  ✓ route comparison — course-anthropic in 121ms
  ✓ route vllm — murshid-onprem in 109ms

all good — you are ready for Lab 1
```

Every cross has a fix on the [troubleshooting page](reference/troubleshooting.qmd).
The two that catch people:

::: {.callout-warning}
## Windows terminals and Arabic

`✗ terminal renders Arabic` means your console is on a code page that cannot encode
Arabic, and half this course's test data is Arabic. Use **Windows Terminal** or the
**VS Code integrated terminal**, and set `PYTHONUTF8=1`. Test it *now* — a
participant discovering this at 09:15 on Day 1 loses the first lab.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## `✗ route ...` — the gateway is not running

`make gateway` in another terminal, or `docker compose up -d gateway`. Every route
points at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` by default.
:::

## Pointing at a real provider

Nothing in the course requires it. When you want it — for the capstone's model
comparison, or because you have keys and would rather use them — it is two
environment variables per route and no code change:

```bash
cp configs/settings.example.env .env

export MURSHID_PRIMARY_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
export MURSHID_PRIMARY_API_KEY=sk-...

make doctor      # the route now names a real model
make eval        # the same 126 cases, the same asserts, different evidence
```

The classroom variant points at the course gateway proxy, which holds the real
provider keys with per-participant budgets — so you never handle a raw key.
That arrangement *is* the reference architecture from Module 1; it is worth
noticing that the classroom is built the way the module says to build.

## What you have installed

| Package | Version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `openai` | 3.8.0 | The OpenAI-compatible adapter — which also covers vLLM and gateways |
| `anthropic` | 1.4.0 | The Messages dialect, whose differences Module 2 dissects |
| `pydantic` | 2.13.5 | The output contracts, and the validators the schema cannot express |
| `langchain-core` | 1.6.2 | Composition only. The logic stays in plain Python |
| `tiktoken` | 0.14.0 | Token counting, per route, with the route's own encoding |
| `structlog` | 26.1.0 | One JSON object per line, so `jq` is the analytics tool |
| `redis` | 8.1.0 | The exact-tier response cache in Lab 6 |
| `fastapi` / `uvicorn` | 0.141.1 / 0.52.4 | The API layer, and the course gateway |

Pinned in `requirements.lock`, and pinned deliberately: floating installs are how a
lab breaks for one pair and not the others, twenty minutes in.

## A note on what the gateway is

The course gateway is a **simulator**, not a model. It speaks both wire dialects
correctly, accounts tokens, caches byte-stable prefixes, injects faults on demand,
and grounds every answer in the service directory that arrives in the prompt — but
the difference in *quality* between its "model tiers" is rules, not capability.

That matters when you write your evaluation report. Numbers measured against it are
true statements about your harness, your guards, your meter and your gates. They
are not evidence about any model. The [gateway reference](reference/gateway.qmd)
says exactly what is real and what is not.
